question: A bag marked at ₹80 is sold for ₹68. The rate of discount is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = **Marked Price (MP) − Selling Price (SP)**

Discount = 80 − 68 = 12

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

Discount % = (12 ÷ 80) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹80, **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹68.
**Formula:** Discount% = ((MP − SP) ÷ MP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e99e1a1e8925e045f813911f000f7d95120a591c194480fb84ecf465ae386f60.png] 
⇒ Amount of **Discount** = MP − SP = 80 − 68 = 12
⇒ **Rate of Discount** = (12 ÷ 80) × 100
⇒ **Rate of Discount** = (3 ÷ 20) × 100
⇒ **Rate of Discount** = 3 × 5 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price unless stated otherwise. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

When two discounts a% and b% are given, the **equivalent single discount** is (a + b − ab/100)%.
